h1: The 6 Best Cordless Chainsaws Under $200 for Yard and Firewood Work, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 6 cordless chainsaws under $200 compared on bar length, brushless power, voltage and batteries included in the box.
summary: The SEESII 40V 16 Inch and 12 Inch kit with two 5.0Ah batteries is the best cordless chainsaw under $200 for most owners, giving two bar sizes and long runtime. The SEESII 40V 16-Inch 2000W brushless is the more powerful single saw, and the Greenworks 40V 12 inch is the brand-backed choice.
intro: Voltage numbers sell cordless chainsaws, and they mislead more than they help. A 20V saw with two 4.0Ah batteries may run longer between charges than a 40V saw with one small battery, because what you actually need is stored energy and a motor that does not waste it. The question to ask is how many amp-hours come in the box and whether the motor is brushless.

This ranking sorts six cordless chainsaws under the $200 mark by bar length, motor type, battery capacity and brand support. We reviewed listing titles and specs, and we left out two Greenworks 80V saws that sit above this budget. Where a listing does not show a feature, we say so, and we do not make up chain speeds or runtimes.

products.name: SEESII 40V 16 Inch & 12 Inch Cordless Electric Chainsaw 2×5.0Ah Batteries
products.verdict: Two bar sizes and two 5.0Ah batteries, the most complete kit under $200.
products.description:
This SEESII 40V kit offers both a 16 inch and a 12 inch bar and ships with two 5.0Ah batteries. Street pricing: $100 to $200.

It takes first place because capacity decides how much work you get done. Two 5.0Ah packs give you one battery to work with while the other charges, which is the difference between finishing a cord of firewood and stopping for lunch. Two bars also let you use a shorter, safer bar for limbing and the longer one for bigger logs. The listing does not show full specifications, so we cannot confirm motor type or oiling.

Buy it if you want one saw for varied jobs and plenty of runtime. Skip it if you need a documented brushless motor.
cons: Motor type not shown in listing
products.idealFor: Homeowners with mixed yard and firewood jobs.
products.skipIf: You want a brushless motor confirmed.

products.name: SEESII 40V 16-Inch Cordless Electric Chainsaw, 2000W Brushless Chain Saw
products.verdict: A 16 inch saw with a 2000W brushless motor, the strongest stated power here.
products.description:
This SEESII 40V saw has a 16 inch bar and a 2000W brushless motor. Street pricing: $100 to $200. The wattage is the highest of any saw in this ranking.

It ranks second because the brushless motor and 16 inch bar suit felling small trees and cutting seasoned logs, and a wattage claim at this level suggests torque in dense wood. It falls behind the two-battery kit because the listing does not say how many batteries are included, and wattage figures on budget saws are best treated as marketing rather than measurement.

Choose it if you want a long bar and a strong motor. Skip it if battery count is critical to you.
products.idealFor: Users who cut dense wood and bigger logs.
products.skipIf: You need to know the battery count.

products.name: Greenworks 40V 12 in Cordless Electric Chainsaw, 2.0 Ah Battery and Charger
products.verdict: A 12 inch Greenworks 40V saw with a battery and charger, backed by an established brand.
products.description:
The Greenworks 40V is a 12 inch cordless saw that includes a 2.0 Ah battery and charger. Street pricing: $100 to $200.

It ranks third because it offers the least stored energy in the box, only 2.0 Ah, but wins on brand support. Greenworks has a long-running 40V range, which makes spare batteries and replacement chains easy to find. A 12 inch bar is a sensible size for limbing, storm clean-up and everyday firewood, and it is easier to control than a 16 inch.

Buy it if you value support and a known brand over capacity. Skip it if you plan long sessions on a single charge.
pros: 12 inch bar is easy to control
products.idealFor: Occasional users who want brand support.
products.skipIf: You need long runtime on one charge.

products.name: 12" Electric Chainsaw Cordless, 20V Battery Powered Cordless Chain Saw, Chainsaw with 2 x 4.0Ah Lithium ion Battery and Charger
products.verdict: A 12 inch 20V saw with two 4.0Ah lithium-ion batteries and a charger for $50 to $100.
products.description:
This 12 inch, 20V chainsaw comes with two 4.0Ah lithium-ion batteries and a charger, aimed at wood cutting, tree trimming and branch pruning. It is in the $50 to $100 price tier.

It ranks fourth because it is the most affordable full kit, with 8.0Ah of stored energy for less money than most single-battery saws. The tradeoff is voltage: a 20V system generally gives less cutting torque than a 40V one, so it is better suited to branches and softwood than to dense hardwood logs. The listing also omits brand details and a motor type.

Buy it for light-to-medium work on a tight budget. Skip it if you regularly cut hardwood.
pros: Lowest price for a full kit
12 inch bar fits most yard jobs
products.idealFor: Budget buyers pruning and cutting softwood.

products.name: SEESII 12-Inch Electric Chainsaw Cordless, Brushless Motor
products.verdict: A 12 inch brushless SEESII saw, priced between $50 and $100.
products.description:
This SEESII saw has a 12 inch bar and a brushless motor, with no further details in the listing. Street pricing: $50 to $100.

It ranks fifth because the listing is lean on the information that matters most, battery count and voltage. The brushless motor is a plus, as it generally means less wasted energy and longer tool life, and a 12 inch bar is a good size for most yard work. Compared with the 20V kit above, it offers a better motor but unknown battery inclusions.

Pick it if you already have SEESII batteries or want a compact brushless saw. Skip it if you want clarity on the battery in the box.
products.idealFor: Owners of SEESII batteries wanting a lighter saw.
products.skipIf: You need a fully described kit.

products.name: ReliaRoads 16 In Brushless Chainsaw, 40V Chainsaw Compatible DeWALT Battery
products.verdict: A 16 inch brushless saw built to take DeWALT batteries. Street pricing: $50 to $100.
products.description:
The ReliaRoads is a 16 inch brushless chainsaw rated at 40V and listed as compatible with DeWALT batteries. Street pricing: $50 to $100.

It ranks last because a battery-compatible bare tool depends on a pack you already own, and the listing does not say which DeWALT packs fit. That detail matters, since a 40V claim on a platform built around 20V packs needs checking. For an owner of suitable DeWALT batteries, though, a 16 inch brushless saw at this price is a bargain.

Buy it if you already own the right DeWALT packs. Skip it if you are starting from nothing.
products.idealFor: DeWALT battery owners wanting a long bar.
products.skipIf: You do not already own batteries.

whatMatters.detail: Amp-hours measure how much energy a battery holds. Two 5.0Ah batteries hold 10Ah in total, about five times what a single 2.0Ah pack offers. On a listing, count the batteries and read the Ah number, because the voltage alone says little about runtime.

Brushless motors need no carbon brushes, produce less heat and waste less energy than brushed ones. That gives longer runtime and a longer tool life. Look for the word brushless in the title, and be cautious of large wattage figures with no maker data to back them.

A 16 inch bar handles larger logs, but it is heavier and harder to control than a 12 inch. For limbing and tidy-up, 12 inch is plenty. Choose the bar for your usual cut, not the biggest job you imagine.

Higher voltage usually means more power available to the motor, so a 40V saw will push through dense wood better than a 20V one. For softwood and branches, 20V is fine. Check the voltage in the product title.

Cordless chainsaws still need bar and chain oil, regular tensioning and a sharp chain. Look for an oil window or auto-oil feature, and keep a spare chain handy. A dull chain is the leading cause of poor cuts.

faq.q: Can a cordless chainsaw replace a gas saw?
faq.a: For yard work, storm cleanup and moderate firewood, yes. For felling large trees or all-day work, a gas saw still wins on runtime. Under $200, think of these as homeowner tools.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake with cordless chainsaws?
faq.a: Buying on voltage alone and ignoring battery capacity. A 20V saw with two 4.0Ah packs can outlast a 40V saw with one 2.0Ah pack, so count the amp-hours.

faq.q: Is the Greenworks 40V worth it over the SEESII kits?
faq.a: If you want brand support and easy spares, yes. For raw value, the SEESII two-battery kit gives far more stored energy and two bars for a similar price tier.
Usually 10 to 15 minutes. Fit the bar and chain, set tension, fill the oil reservoir and charge a battery. Check that the chain is facing the right direction.

faq.q: How do I maintain the chain?
faq.a: Keep the chain sharp, tensioned and oiled, and clean sawdust from the bar groove after use. Store batteries partly charged and away from extreme heat or cold.
Yes. Wear cut-resistant gloves, eye and ear protection, sturdy boots and, for larger saws, chaps. Cordless saws are quieter, but they cut as fast as petrol ones.

finalTake: For most owners the SEESII 40V 16 Inch and 12 Inch kit with two 5.0Ah batteries is the best cordless chainsaw under $200, with the most stored energy and two bar sizes. The SEESII 2000W brushless is the stronger single saw, and the Greenworks 40V is the brand-backed pick. If you only prune, the 20V two-battery kit is plenty.
